This lesson executes the same R functions as the one-command workflow. Start
from the project root. Its outputs are isolated in `results/notebook_demo/`.
The dataset has one healthy donor; all automatic annotations remain candidates.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
source("scripts/bootstrap.R")
check_packages()
cfg <- load_config("config/config.R")
cfg$output_dir <- "results/notebook_demo"
ensure_output(cfg)
set.seed(cfg$seed)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, warning = TRUE)
```

## 1. Import raw counts

A count matrix contains integer UMI observations. Genes are rows and cells are
columns in Seurat. The demo verifies the bundled checksums before importing.

```{r import}
stage_ingest(cfg)
pbmc <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "ingest"))
dim(pbmc)
sum(raw_counts(pbmc))
head(pbmc[[]])
```

**Question:** Why must normalized values not be supplied as raw counts?

## 2. Quality control and doublets

The pipeline applies a minimum-gene screen, predicts doublets separately within
the capture, then applies the remaining QC thresholds. Each cell receives an
audit row. A high score is a prediction, not proof of a doublet.

```{r quality-control, message=FALSE}
stage_qc(cfg)
audit <- read.csv(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "tables/cell_qc.csv"))
table(audit$qc_keep)
sort(table(audit$removal_reason), decreasing = TRUE)
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "figures/qc.png")), rel_path = FALSE)
```

**Question:** How could strict mitochondrial filtering remove a real cell state?

## 3. Normalize and find variable genes

LogNormalize divides by the cell's library size, scales to 10,000 and applies
log1p. VST identifies variable genes. Scaling is restricted to variable features.
The raw RNA count layer remains unchanged.

```{r normalize, message=FALSE}
stage_normalize(cfg)
pbmc <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "normalize"))
head(SeuratObject::VariableFeatures(pbmc))
SeuratObject::Layers(pbmc[["RNA"]])
```

**Question:** Why retain raw counts after creating normalized values?

## 4. PCA, graph clustering and UMAP

PCA summarizes scaled expression. Neighbors and Louvain clustering define
groups. UMAP uses the R uwot implementation and visualizes local relationships.

```{r reduce, message=FALSE}
stage_reduce(cfg)
pbmc <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "reduce"))
Seurat::ElbowPlot(pbmc)
Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = "cluster", label = TRUE)
```

**Question:** How might PCA dimension choice and clustering resolution alter
the groups? Does a gap in UMAP prove a distinct biological lineage?

## 5. Find cluster markers

Wilcoxon tests compare each cluster to the other cells. Positive marker
selection follows testing. Seurat's adjusted marker p-values use Bonferroni
correction. These exploratory comparisons are not donor-level disease tests.

```{r markers, message=FALSE}
stage_markers(cfg)
markers <- read.csv(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "tables/markers_top10.csv"))
knitr::kable(head(markers, 15), digits = 3)
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "figures/marker_dotplot.png")), rel_path = FALSE)
```

**Question:** Why is one marker insufficient to label every cluster?

## 6. Review candidate annotations

Panel scores are heuristics. Inspect multiple lineage markers and conflicting
evidence. NKG7 and PRF1 can appear in cytotoxic T cells as well as NK cells.
Candidate T/NK labels therefore also consider CD3D, CD3E, TRAC, GNLY and KLRD1.

```{r annotate, message=FALSE}
stage_annotate(cfg)
pbmc <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "annotate"))
Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type")
knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "tables/annotation_evidence.csv")), digits = 3)
```

**Question:** Which clusters need the most careful review before accepting labels?

## 7. Reactome enrichment

Over-representation compares top positive markers to each cluster's tested-gene
background. BH correction includes all eligible pathways, including zero
overlaps. Enrichment does not establish pathway activation or causality.

```{r enrichment, message=FALSE}
stage_enrich(cfg)
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "figures/enrichment.png")), rel_path = FALSE)
```

**Question:** Why would using every human gene as background change the result?

## 8. Save a report and check raw counts

The report embeds its figures and opens offline. Intermediate RDS objects,
full tables, settings and software versions remain available for inspection.

```{r report, message=FALSE}
stage_report(cfg)
input <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "ingest"))
expected <- raw_counts(input)[rownames(pbmc), colnames(pbmc), drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(Matrix::nnzero(raw_counts(pbmc) - expected) == 0)
knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "provenance/package_versions.csv")))
sessionInfo()
```

PBMC3k has one donor and cannot demonstrate a disease/control contrast. The
separate DESeq2 extension requires reviewed cell labels and independent donors.
See `docs/04_multisample.md` before adapting it to a real study.
